title: orders-api — write-side HTTP service for customer orders
notes: Mixed by design. q2, q3, q4, q6 and q7 are answerable and citable from the readme and the manifest alone, so a competent shallow system can score on them. q5 is documented nowhere but the code: any system that answers it from shallow context is guessing, and can at best earn existence-level credit from the directory listing. The gap between those two groups is the headroom the advanced agent has to close.

questions.question: What does this service do, and is it on the read side or the write side of the ordering system?
questions.expectedAnswer: It is the write side: it accepts customer orders over HTTP, validates, prices and reserves them, and publishes an order.created event. Reads are served by a separate reporting service.

questions.question: Which HTTP framework does the service use?
questions.expectedAnswer: Express (declared as a runtime dependency in package.json).

questions.question: How does the service tell other systems that an order was created?
questions.expectedAnswer: It publishes an order.created event to Kafka, via the kafkajs producer in src/lib/events.js.

questions.question: Which routes require authentication, and which are exempt?
questions.expectedAnswer: Every route except /health requires a bearer JWT, verified in src/middleware/auth.js against JWT_SECRET.

questions.question: What stops two concurrent orders from overselling the same SKU?
questions.expectedAnswer: reserveInventory runs inside a transaction and locks the inventory row with SELECT available ... FOR UPDATE before decrementing it. Nothing in the readme or the manifest says so; it is only visible in src/services/inventory.js and the incident note in docs/incidents/.

questions.question: What is the largest gap in this repository's test coverage?
questions.expectedAnswer: There are no integration tests: the Postgres and Kafka clients are never exercised, so src/lib/db.js and src/lib/events.js are untested.

questions.question: What kind of API does the service expose?
questions.expectedAnswer: A JSON HTTP API built on Express, with POST /orders as the only write path and GET /health as a public probe.
